0.0.n: The て-form of 見る is used alone here as a casual request.

0.2.n: Names the body of water where the town appears to float.

0.3.n: Marks the sea as the place where the town floats.

0.4.n: The plain form directly describes 街, telling us what kind of town it is.

0.5.n: Refers to the built-up settlement, rather than an individual street.

0.6.n: Adds emphasis when pointing something out; directly after a noun like this, it has a feminine conversational feel.

1.0.n: The speaker names herself as the topic, leaving out the usual topic particle は.

1.2.n: This is the speaker’s name, written in katakana.

1.3.n: Politely completes the self-introduction after the speaker’s name.

0.lit: Look! Sea-on floating town, I tell you!
0.tip: 海に浮かぶ comes before 街 and describes it: a town that floats on the sea.

1.tip: In conversation, は is often omitted after 私 when introducing yourself.
